report:
PASS applies only to the restricted A–G extension. Original S11 remains open. I independently assessed the complete current article, the retained wording replacement, the historical draft and private pole-center proof, the complete F–G supplement, the ruled-family article, the scoped reviews, and every reconstruction note in both supplied graphs. Prior verdicts, candidate flags, hashes, build records and numerical diagnostics were not mathematical premises.

A. The regularization application satisfies all hypotheses. T=dd^c q' is closed and almost positive; its smooth closed representative is 0, its source potential is ψ=q'/2, and its continuous lower bound is γ=εh−B. Thus the source operator (i/π)∂bar∂ produces exactly the task current. Compactness bounds the selected tangent metric's Griffiths curvature below by −Ch⊗Id, so u=Ch satisfies the stronger curvature hypothesis. Zero Lelong numbers make E_s(T) empty for every fixed s>0. The continuous decreasing λ_k converge uniformly to zero by Dini, and ε_k tends to zero. Choosing k with C sup λ_k+ε_k≤ε/2 gives the globally smooth f=2ψ_(s,k) and B+dd^c f≥εh/2. The reconstruction's alternative fixed choice s=ε/(4C) also supplies a uniform loss. Neither argument establishes f∼q', and neither regularizes the nonclosed current B+dd^c q'. The supplied complete Section 2 proof uses Richberg only on continuous intermediates. The university PDF timed out during fresh retrieval; the matching [author-uploaded primary paper](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/247379399_Regularization_of_Closed_Positive_Currents_and_Intersection_Theory) was opened. No PDF byte identity is inferred.

E. The same-type antecedent is used exactly as stated. For each actual q_δ, T_δ=dd^c q_δ+δh is positive. In dimension n≥2, the Gauduchon metric gives the exact distributional identity ∫T_δ∧γ^(n−1)=δ∫h∧γ^(n−1). This does not require T_δ to be closed. Fixed quadratics on finitely many nested coordinate charts give genuine psh p_δ=q_δ+δρ, whose Hessians are closed and positive. The identity dd^c p_δ=T_δ+δ(dd^cρ−h), smooth metric comparison and finite chart volumes bound their local Euclidean traces by Cδ, independently of the representative. Fixed admissible radii then bound every point Lelong number by C'δ. The trace theorem is applied with bidimension n−1. For n=1, bidimension zero identifies the Lelong number with an atom, bounded by the total positive measure δ∫h; equivalently γ^0=1 handles Stokes directly. Smooth additions and mutual bounded order preserve the logarithmic coefficient. The source-to-task factor is 2, so it changes only fixed constants. Letting δ tend to zero proves vanishing at every point. This establishes the antecedent required by the new B; the historical additional zero-Lelong assumption is not inherited. The complete supplied proofs match [Gauduchon's Theorem 2](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf) and the specified [Demailly local trace and growth foundations](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

Canonical extension and B. After omitting zero coefficients, subtract the logarithmic potential only off its support. Locally, v+ρ−Σa_j log|g_j|² is psh and locally bounded above by the ordinary comparison with q. Canonical removability supplies the residual extension. Its positive Hessian has positive coefficient-matrix measures on the divisor, while the smooth lower bound has zero measure restriction there. Consequently the sharp inequality B+dd^c q'≥εh survives globally, including when B is nonclosed. Recovery of canonical psh values by ball averages, or the reconstruction's outside-set limsup argument, extends both inequalities q'≤q+C and q≤q'+C at every pole. Canonical equality also identifies v with ell_Δ+q'. E gives zero Lelong numbers, and A supplies the smooth positive gauge. Conversely, a smooth gauge has a uniform positive margin on compact M. An actual same-type q_δ with curvature loss below half that margin makes ell_Δ+q_δ+f strict by Poincaré–Lelong. Both ordinary inequalities remain valid where the logarithmic term or residual is −∞. Zero divisor terms are genuine zero functions. No pole-bearing current is restricted to a divisor.

F. Local smooth corrections express the canonical pullback as a holomorphic pullback of psh functions. Every source open set meets the modification's isomorphism locus, so these functions are locally nontrivial and integrable. Both ordinary inequalities compose pointwise, including poles. The sharp bound −δπ*h holds on the isomorphism locus and extends across the exceptional analytic set by the same positive coefficient-measure argument. Compactness gives the smooth semipositive, possibly degenerate, bound π*h≤Ch'. Choosing δ arbitrarily small establishes the actual same-type antecedent upstairs. Applying E on M' proves zero Lelong numbers everywhere. No factorization or general preservation theorem for arbitrary zero-Lelong pullbacks is needed.

C. Both residual constructions are valid. The author's piecewise χ_L matches value and derivative at −L, is convex increasing, and has derivative between zero and η_L→0. Its singular tail differs from U by a finite constant. The reconstruction's shifted power L^α−(L−G_p)^α satisfies the explicit inequalities U≤U_L≤U+L^α−1 and has curvature loss αL^(α−1). These are genuine same-type representatives with the same poles. Canonical extension retains their curvature inequalities, and actual pullback bounds the loss by Cη_Lh'. At every total-transform point, its nonzero holomorphic equation has finite order N. A direction with nonzero leading term gives log|g(tξ)|²=2N log|t|+O(1), hence a spherical supremum bounded below by −C|log r|^α−C. After a smooth psh correction, division by the negative logarithm forces the nonnegative Lelong coefficient to zero. Away from the divisor the function is smooth. The reconstruction's monomial chart induction independently covers every infinitely near point and every finite depth.

D. B applies to bπ*D and residual π*U. The residual background is π*β. The final exceptional curve is smooth and contracted by the composite map. Only a hypothetical smooth gauge f is restricted to it: π*β vanishes tangentially, so strict positivity would give dd^c(f|E)>0, contradicting curve Stokes. This proves the obstruction at all stated centers, including poles.

The recursive one-sided witness has an actual Hermitian margin at each stage. O(E)|E=O(−1) permits curvature B_E negative on the exceptional tangent. In bounded blowup charts the pullback metric has a uniformly positive horizontal entry, mixed entry O(|x|), and Schur complement at least c|x|². Subtracting tB_E adds a positive vertical term; fixing the neighborhood and then taking t small controls the errors t|x|, t|x|² and t². Compactness controls the complement. The reconstruction's compact unit-tangent-bundle proof independently establishes the same positivity: the correction is positive on the zero locus of the semipositive pullback form. Adding the corresponding positive exceptional logarithm therefore restores strictness recursively. Pullbacks and sums remain genuine over pole centers. Globally upper-bounded logarithms preserve v'≤π*r+C. The added exceptional coefficient, and independently the obstruction, excludes mutual ordinary equivalence. Separately, the specified full-competitor bijection and actual mass pushforward preserve the extrema of the original pulled-back type, giving 2(c−b)min a and 2(c−b)max a. The witness's new type is never substituted into that optimization.

G. The integrability proof does not assume the desired conclusion. On a bounded pseudoconvex chart, correct q to psh φ and fix any real m>0. Its weighted Hilbert unit ball has uniformly bounded local first derivatives: an upper bound on φ controls the local unweighted L² norm, followed by mean-value and Cauchy estimates. If every weighted holomorphic function vanished at x, the evaluation kernel would satisfy K_m(z)≤C|z−x|². Thus φ_m≤m^(-1)log|z−x|+O(1), giving ν(φ_m,x)≥1/m, contrary to the Bergman bound ν(φ_m,x)≤ν(φ,x)=0. An actual weighted function is therefore nonzero at x and bounded away from zero after shrinking. Its finite weighted norm proves integrability of exp(−2mφ). Taking 2m=s and undoing bounded smooth corrections proves every positive exponential weight.

For neutrality, q's local upper bound gives I(t(v+q))⊂I(tv). Strong openness applied to the corrected v with c=t/2 supplies p>1 with |g|²exp(−ptv) integrable. With p'=p/(p−1), the first result and boundedness of g make |g|²exp(−p'tq) integrable. Hölder applies to the exact factorization (|g|²exp(−ptv))^(1/p)(|g|²exp(−p'tq))^(1/p')=|g|²exp(−t(v+q)). The reconstruction's alternative factorization using bounded |g|^(2p−2) is also valid. This proves equality at every stalk and every real t>0, including arbitrary effective divisors. The complete supplied [Bergman and strong-openness proof chain](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.5432v2) was assessed with its stated inherited foundations.

For the SNC formula, transverse order k is integrable precisely when k+1>ta_j. Hence the minimum order is floor(ta_j); at an integer endpoint the previous order has the divergent radial exponent −1. Necessity follows from a nonzero leading tangential coefficient and Fubini; dividing by the required coordinate powers leaves all exponents integrable. Only positive-coefficient components enter restricted equations. Noncontainment and connectedness make each restricted equation nonzero; dominance of every modification preserves that property. Its divisorial order N_j is finite. The exact ideal order is Σ floor(ta_j)N_j, with error from its limiting value bounded by ΣN_j/t. Thus every displayed intrinsic trace exists and is finite. These are restricted ambient ideals, even when q|Y≡−∞; neither naive-restriction ideals nor envelope lower inequalities are substituted.

Supporting ruled-family proofs. The complete retained article was freshly fetched at the specified commit. Canonical divisor removal and fiber averaging exclude b≥c; both residual constructions give strict same-type representatives whenever b<c. For every rough residual competitor, the auxiliary currents K+dd^c q and the separated reference are closed, positive and cohomologous on the compact Kähler ruled surface, locally bounded outside the closed locally complete pluripolar divisor D. Thus [BEGZ comparison](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf) applies in both ordinary orders and degrees one and two. Degree one removes the positive polar defect through its zero K-trace; degree two establishes full auxiliary closed mass. The finite smooth-background expansion then gives M(v)=∫β²+2∫q dd^cβ=2∫aσ, where σ is positive of mass c−b. Both extremizing constructions are actual same-type competitors, including concentration at p. No nonlinear first moment is required. Sphere potentials can be realized by smooth Green-kernel integration.

The supporting transverse ideal endpoints, genuine descent and mass pushforward, both outside-pole blowup witnesses, and their justified bounded restrictions are correct. The separated first-moment tail is 2Cα(1−α)T^(2α−2), giving exactly the stated threshold and divergence constants. Both Gauduchon-volume proofs cover all mixed and fiber-dependent tests, attain the quotient, and give the signed derivative and integrated subtraction identity. Smooth and divisor-metric gauges preserve the appropriate currents, ordinary types, masses and ideal traces. The explicit nonclosed example has margin 3/8 for the shifted reference, mass pair (3/2,9/2), and the stated intrinsic orders. BGL's existing definitions and modification/divisor credit remain separate; no additional broad theorem from that citation is needed.

Dependency audit. Distinguishing the historical ruled notes H from extension notes N, the historical graph is H1; H2←H1; H3←H1; H4←H1,H2,H3; H5←H1,H2,H3; H6←H2; H7←H1,…,H6. The extension graph is N1; N2←N1; N3←N1; N4←N1; N5←N1,N2,N3,N4; N6←N2,N3; N7←N1,N2; N8←N1,N2,N5,N7; N9←N1,N3; N10←N1,…,N9. Its 26 edges are backward and all parent proofs are available and valid; redundant edges are harmless. Mathematically A uses regularization; E uses Gauduchon and local trace/growth; F uses canonical pullback and E; B uses divisor removal, E and A; C uses explicit tails and growth; D uses B, C, exceptional metrics and the separately credited mass laws; G uses Bergman, openness and the SNC calculation. No unrelated companion coefficient or envelope assertion enters this DAG.

Qualifications and evidence. The source8830fc narrowing of conformal uniqueness to n≥2 is harmless: n=1 was already proved separately. The frozen historical convolution identity is exact for quadratic corrections; for general smooth k it requires the additional uniformly vanishing term (dd^c k)*ρ_ε−dd^c k. Bergman kernel convergence is needed on compact subsets. The openness proof uses bounds above, subsequences for general pointwise and sliced convergence, and f_l in place of the displayed 1; its actual scaling application has the required convergence directly. Richberg is used only on continuous intermediates. Additionally, the dominated-convergence step in the displayed BEGZ Lemma 1.5 requires pointwise exhaustion; the increasing level sets actually used satisfy it, so its unrestricted arbitrary-sequence wording is not imported. These qualifications require no substantial repair of A–G.

The earlier short quotation fragments do not substantiate their full indexed premises. The eight bindings below replace them with complete verbatim task foundations, each exactly equal to its indexed premise. Matching primary sources were opened and the supplied complete printed contexts assessed. Ohsawa–Takegoshi, Kiselman, Richberg, analytic division and Bedford–Taylor retain their permitted imported status; their deeper proofs are not recursively certified. This PASS establishes neither unrestricted S11, a general modification factorization, an arbitrary-density volume law, nor a universal residual-mass strictness criterion.

passages.statement: Demailly’s 1992 Main Theorem 1.1, with its Section 2 stronger curvature hypothesis, states: on a compact Hermitian manifold (M,h), let T=α+(i/π)∂bar∂ψ be a closed almost positive real (1,1)-current, with α smooth closed real and ψ genuine quasi-psh, and let γ be any continuous real (1,1)-form satisfying T≥γ. If a selected smooth tangent metric has Griffiths curvature c(TM)+u⊗Id≥0 for a smooth semipositive form u, then for every s>0 there are global potentials ψ_(s,k), smooth on M\{ν(T,·)≥s}, satisfying α+(i/π)∂bar∂ψ_(s,k)≥γ−min(λ_k,s)u−ε_kh, where λ_k are continuous and decrease pointwise to ν(T,·), and ε_k>0 decreases to zero. γ need not be closed.

passages.statement: Gauduchon’s standard-metric theorem states that on a connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension n≥2, every smooth Hermitian metric is conformal to a smooth positive Hermitian form γ satisfying dd^cγ^(n−1)=0, unique in its conformal class up to positive scalar multiplication.

passages.statement: For a closed positive current T of bidimension (p,p) on a coordinate domain in C^n, 0≤p≤n, define σ_T=(1/p!)T∧((i/2)∂bar∂|z|²)^p. For coordinate balls contained in the domain, σ_T(B(x,r))/(π^p r^(2p)/p!) is nondecreasing in r and tends to ν(T,x) as r decreases to zero; in particular ν(T,x) is bounded above by this ratio at any fixed admissible radius.

passages.statement: Demailly’s arXiv:1401.5432v2 Theorem 1.2 states: for a genuine psh φ on a bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω⊂C^n and every real m>0, let H_Ω(mφ) consist of holomorphic functions with finite integral ∫_Ω|g|²e^(−2mφ)dV. passages.statement: Guan–Zhou strong openness, as stated in Demailly’s arXiv:1401.5432v2 Corollary 2.3 with the supplied Hiep proof, states: if φ is genuine psh near x, g is holomorphic near x, c>0, and |g|²e^(−2cφ) is locally integrable near x, then there exists c'>c for which |g|²e^(−2c'φ) is integrable on a possibly smaller neighborhood of x.

passages.statement: For 1≤p≤n, non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on a compact Kähler n-manifold are well defined, positive, closed and of finite mass, and put no mass on pluripolar sets. They are local in the plurifine topology. For potentials locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement. Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ. These are BEGZ §1.2, Proposition 1.6 and Theorem 1.8.

passages.statement: BEGZ Theorem 1.16 states: on a compact Kähler n-manifold, for 1≤p≤n, let T_j and T'_j be cohomologous closed positive (1,1)-currents with small unbounded locus, meaning local boundedness of potentials outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set. If every T_j is less singular than T'_j in ordinary bounded order, then {⟨T_1∧…∧T_p⟩}−{⟨T'_1∧…∧T'_p⟩} is represented by a closed positive (p,p)-current.

For a closed positive current T of bidimension (p,p) on a coordinate domain in C^n, 0≤p≤n, define σ_T=(1/p!)T∧((i/2)∂bar∂|z|²)^p. For coordinate balls contained in the domain, σ_T(B(x,r))/(π^p r^(2p)/p!) is nondecreasing in r and tends to ν(T,x) as r decreases to zero; in particular ν(T,x) is bounded above by this ratio at any fixed admissible radius.

For 1≤p≤n, non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on a compact Kähler n-manifold are well defined, positive, closed and of finite mass, and put no mass on pluripolar sets. They are local in the plurifine topology. For potentials locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement. Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ. These are BEGZ §1.2, Proposition 1.6 and Theorem 1.8.
